headline: Tokyo disembarkation and flight home
summary: Tokyo should be sunny and dry for disembarkation. The main risk is time: a tentative Skytree/Aquarium visit must fit between the ship's 8 AM arrival and a 4:25 PM international flight. Typhoon In-fa remains far south, with rough seas near Ogasawara but no verified impact on Tokyo.

details: JMA Tokyo forecast issued October 30 at 5 PM JST: sunny with occasional clouds; 0% chance of rain from 6 AM–noon and 10% from noon–6 PM.
No expected rain window during disembarkation, Skytree sightseeing or the Haneda transfer. This is a six-hour-area forecast, not a precise hourly guarantee.

sources.label: JMA Tokyo forecast, October 30 (reported by FNN)

items: 8:00 AM — Scheduled Seven Seas Explorer arrival at Tokyo International Cruise Terminal, Odaiba; disembarkation time to be confirmed onboard.
9:00 AM–12:30 PM — Tentative Tokyo Skytree / Sumida Aquarium sightseeing, 1-1-2 Oshiage, Sumida City. Calendar description says 'if confirmed'; not a booked commitment.
4:25 PM JST — Delta flight from Haneda Airport to Seattle (scheduled arrival 9:25 AM PDT, October 31).
plans.note: The sightseeing window is tight once disembarkation, luggage, cross-city travel and airport transfer are considered. Delta recommends reaching the airport three hours before international departure: target 1:25 PM. Prefer only one attraction or skip sightseeing if luggage or disembarkation runs late. No rain conflict is anticipated.

next.summary: Sunday, November 1 · Trip complete; no further cruise port
details: No November 1 events found on the secondary Outlook calendar 'Kyle'.
The October 31 Haneda–Seattle flight is scheduled to arrive in Seattle on October 31 local time; no further Japan port or excursion.

typhoon.status: No significant typhoon threat to upcoming ports
typhoon.summary: In-fa remains a very strong typhoon over the Ogasawara waters, far south of mainland Tokyo. The ship's Tokyo approach and Haneda departure have low direct typhoon exposure; distant ocean swell is possible but no Regent-confirmed change was found.
details: Latest directly verified JMA advisory: October 31, 3:50 AM JST (3:00 AM observation): 20.5°N, 143.4°E; 940 hPa; maximum sustained winds 45 m/s (162 km/h), gusts 65 m/s (234 km/h); northwest at 25 km/h.
Weathernews' 6:00 AM JST JMA-based update places In-fa near 20°50′N, 143°00′E, still 940 hPa and moving west-northwest at 20 km/h.
Change since October 30 morning: shifted northwest from around 17.5°N, 148.6°E, while central pressure and sustained winds remain approximately unchanged at 940 hPa and 45 m/s.
Forecast: slow and turn near waters south of the Ogasawara Islands through November 1–3, with hazardous surf there. Longer-range movement uncertain; confidence lower after November 1.
Champi became extratropical October 25 and is no longer a typhoon. No remaining cruise ports after Tokyo; no verified Regent routing or port changes. Follow ship announcements.

sources.label: JMA advisory reproduced by Applied Meteorological Engineering

headsUp: Tokyo International Cruise Terminal's October 30 notice schedules Seven Seas Explorer arrival at approximately 8:00 AM October 31; times may change. Levels 2 and 3 are restricted to ship users.
Delta recommends arrival at Haneda at least three hours before international departure: about 1:25 PM for a 4:25 PM flight.
No other major verified disruption affecting Tokyo sightseeing or the flight was identified.
worthALook: Recurring — Tokyo Skytree, 1-1-2 Oshiage, Sumida: Saturday opening around 9 AM; observation decks and city views. Choose this OR the aquarium to preserve airport buffer.
Recurring — Sumida Aquarium, Skytree Town Solamachi floors 5–6, Oshiage: Saturday hours 9 AM–9 PM; indoor family-friendly alternative.

Dated, final day October 31 — Chiikawa: Starry SKYTREE and the Secret Island, Tokyo Skytree Tembo Deck and Tembo Galleria. Observation deck admission required; cafe access has advance-ticket restrictions.
